value.body: Hotel sales executives bring business into a hotel: corporate room contracts, conferences, weddings and group bookings. They meet clients, prepare proposals, negotiate rates and hand bookings over to operations. Work is target-driven and involves a lot of calls, visits and follow-ups.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BHM, BBA, or a tourism degree

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: Sales executive, sales coordinator, banquet sales associate

items.label: Foreign tourist arrivals
items.source: Ministry of Tourism, reply in Parliament (as reported)

items.label: Domestic tourist visits
items.note: Visits reported by States/UTs; one person can make many visits

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start as sales coordinators supporting a sales team, or move into sales after a stint in front office or F&B. Confident communication and comfort with targets matter more than a specific specialisation.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Knowledge of the hotel's products and rates

value.title: At a glance
items: Pay often includes incentives linked to targets.
Common next steps: sales manager, revenue manager, or director of sales.
Wedding and conference seasons drive busy periods.

value.note: Counts students across all years of the B.H.M. programme only; B.H.M.C.T. and other hotel degrees are counted separately. Based on institutions that reported to AISHE, so year-to-year changes partly reflect reporting.
